text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm going to cancel tonight's full-scale Locust replay for the perf cluster. There's an infra maintenance window that landed on the same hosts. We should instead do a focussed dry-run + profiling session tomorrow morning.

raj: good call. do we want a short dry-run tonight instead or fully cancel?

maria: fully cancel for tonight. we can still run a 15m headless dry-run in perf-staging at 09:30 PT tomorrow to validate traffic shape and our new batching changes. I'm asking for volunteers to own: start the run, grab NVidia traces (if any), collect pprof endpoints, and archive logs.

olivia: I can take ownership of the Locust headless run. I'll start at 09:30 and post artifacts to the perf bucket.

andrew: I'll handle kernel/proc perf capture + flamegraphs. plan: run `sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 900` on the target worker and `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > perf.svg`. Will that work with our containerized workers?

lin: small note — if workers are in containers we should use perf inside the host or enable PERF_EVENT_PARANOID=1 and mount /proc properly. alternatively use nsys for GPU traces: `nsys profile -o capture --trace=cuda,osrt --target-processes=all -- python3 worker.py`

maria: nice. olivia, please disable autoscaling & burst pools for the dry-run so we don't accidentally chew through dedicated capacity. set a strict abort condition: 95th latency > 2s or error rate > 1% for 5 consecutive minutes.

olivia: will do. Also planning a warmup prefix replay to populate KV cache for 5m before ramp. command I'll run: 
```
locust -f tests/locustfile.py --headless -u 200 -r 20 --run-time 15m --host https://perf-api.staging --only-summary --csv=tmp/locust_dryrun
```

raj: for profiling endpoints, can we enable `--pprof-port=6060` on runtime side? we'll need the pprof heap/CPU dumps. Also ensure metrics pipeline has the `request_id` tag so traces correlate.

maria: yes — I've pushed a quick flag to the staging deployment: `--pprof-port=6060` and validated ingress. olivia, when you start, hit `/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30` for a 30s CPU profile and upload the .pb.gz to the perf bucket.

andrew: reminder to capture KV cache hit metrics and token-level batching stats (token_latency_histogram, batch_size_distribution). those are necessary to evaluate the batching change.

perf-bot: Scheduled run cancelled by infra-maintenance (ticket INFRA-5212). New dry-run assigned to @olivia at 2025-08-18T16:30:00Z (09:30 PT).

olivia: thumbs-up. I'll post a summary here after the run with: 1) locust summary csv, 2) pprof CPU profile, 3) perf flamegraph, 4) batch_size_distribution snapshot, 5) any regression notes.

raj: one more ask — if anyone sees a recurring EOF or 502 during the warmup, capture the worker logs with `journalctl -u runtime-worker -n 500` and paste a trimmed excerpt.

maria: perfect. thanks everyone. tagging @andrew and @raj for the trace collection checklist. If anything changes on infra side I'll update this thread. :thumbsup:
